- Overestimate prices when sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.7) and recent prices are rising — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is neutral or negative (e.g., <0.3) — model fails to capture downward pressure.
- Lagged price movements are often over-predicted in the short-term forecast — model reacts too slowly to recent sentiment shifts.
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overcorrect downward — forecast dips too early or too far.
- Mean reversion is overemphasized — model assumes prices return to historical mean too aggressively, ignoring sentiment-driven momentum.
- Forecast horizon 30d is overly sensitive to recent sentiment — if sentiment is volatile, model overfits to short-term noise.
- When sentiment is high but prices are flat, model often assumes continuation and overestimates — should adjust downward if sentiment is “sustained” but no price momentum.
